concepts.title: The Doorbell Camera
concepts.premise: A night nurse's doorbell camera records a hooded figure on her porch every night at 3:12. The recordings carry tomorrow's date.
cast: Mara Quill: night nurse who lives alone and wants a rational answer
Hale Prentiss: elderly neighbor who sees more than he says
The figure: someone who always stands with its back to the door
concepts.setting: A quiet suburban street and the county hospital where Mara works nights
beats: The camera pings at 3:12 and shows a motionless hooded figure on the porch.
The alerts continue, and wet footprints appear on the dry porch.
Mara learns the recordings come from tomorrow and that the reply to her note is in her own handwriting.
She runs, hurts her hand, and sees the same bandage on the figure.
She stands on the porch herself and learns the figures take turns waiting for the next one.
concepts.why_it_works: One ordinary object, one clear rule, and every part can answer one question while raising another.
concepts.audience: Listeners who like quiet, rule-based horror they can follow while doing something else.
concepts.series_potential: Each part follows one night of the loop and reveals one more rule, so the series can run many parts and pay off when Mara breaks the pattern.
risks: Surveillance footage could read as real: never call the recordings real or leaked.
Hospital setting: keep medical details vague so it never reads as advice.

concepts.title: The Last Ferry Light
concepts.premise: A ferry pilot finds that the lighthouse on the far shore blinks a pattern that spells the names of people who have not been born yet.
cast: Ines Moreau: ferry pilot who keeps a logbook of every crossing
Dov Aldren: lighthouse keeper who has not left the island in years
A child's voice on the radio: asks for a name to be added
concepts.setting: A foggy island ferry route and a stone lighthouse
beats: Ines notices the light blinking a pattern that is not on any chart.
She decodes it as names and finds her own sister's unborn child among them.
Dov admits that the light only blinks names it intends to keep.
Ines tries to switch the light off and the names on the list start to change.
She chooses to add a name of her own to save one from the list.
concepts.why_it_works: A decoding puzzle gives every part a concrete discovery and an emotional stake.
concepts.audience: Listeners who like mystery with a human heart.
concepts.series_potential: Each part decodes one more name, and the list gives the series a built-in countdown.
risks: Unborn children and death: keep it implied and never graphic.

concepts.title: Night Shift Backup
concepts.premise: A data-center technician discovers that the nightly backup contains tomorrow's files, and that one of them is a recording of her own funeral.
cast: Priya Landon: technician on the lonely night shift
Gus Whitlow: day manager who insists nothing is wrong
The backup: a file set that grows by one each night
concepts.setting: A windowless server room and the empty office floor above it
beats: Priya finds a folder dated tomorrow in the nightly backup.
The files match events that then happen exactly as written.
She finds a file named after her and cannot open it.
She tries to corrupt the backup and the files rewrite themselves.
She opens the file and learns the backup is trying to warn her, not predict her.
concepts.why_it_works: A workplace setting that is easy to film and a rule that escalates cleanly.
concepts.audience: Listeners who like techno-thrillers with a human twist.
concepts.series_potential: Each part opens one more file, which gives a clear unit of story per part.
risks: Funeral content: keep it to a quiet implied scene.
